question: The jelly-like substance between the nucleus and cell membrane is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cytoplasm is a jelly-like substance that fills the cell between the cell membrane and the nucleus.
 
• It consists of cytosol (the fluid part), organelles, and various particles.
 
• The cytoplasm is where most cellular activities occur, including metabolic pathways such as glycolysis and processes like cell division.
 
• It helps in the movement of materials around the cell and provides a medium for the organelles to remain suspended.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Membrane:**

 
 
• The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, is a biological membrane that separates the interior of all cells from the outside environment.
 
• It is selectively permeable to ions and organic molecules and controls the movement of substances in and out of cells.
 
• The cell membrane is involved in a variety of cellular processes such as cell adhesion, ion conductivity, and cell signaling.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus:**
 
 
• The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It contains most of the cell's genetic material organized as multiple long linear DNA molecules in complex with a large variety of proteins to form chromosomes.
 
• The nucleus maintains the integrity of these genes and controls the activities of the cell by regulating gene expression.
 
 
 
• **Organelles:**
 
 
• Organelles are specialized subunits within a cell that have specific functions, and they are usually separately enclosed within their own lipid bilayers.
 
• Examples include the nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and chloroplasts (in plants).
 
• Each type of organelle has its own role in the cell, such as energy production, protein synthesis, and waste removal.
